intro.lede: The way we work is changing, with AI in its foundations, and it's easier to learn together than alone. The Upskilling Labs is a free community where you find people near you, build something real, and grow more confident together.
intro.terms: One Upskilling account, whichever path you take.
intro.note: Creates your free Upskilling account, with Google: Slack, events, and you can apply.
intro.$people: The faces are the Inaugural AI Cohort's portraits (OLOS public/assets/cohort-grid-sample.png); the count is the DC Lab's on Sep 29, 2026. In OLOS, both from its members.

facts.title: A new way to learn, together.

items.title: Free, always.
items.body: Workshops and Build Cycles cost nothing.

items.title: Rooted in your library.
items.body: In person at your local Lab, with sessions online too.

items.title: No tech background.
items.body: Just a willingness to learn by doing, alongside others.

items.title: Built in the open.
items.body: Everything we make is open source, free for anyone to use and build on.

how.title: One account. Then build something, and pass it on.

steps.title: Create your account.
steps.body: Free, with Google. You get Slack, events and a profile, and you can apply.

steps.title: Drop into a workshop.
steps.body: Weekly at the library, some online. Anyone can come; most people start here.

steps.title: Apply for a Build Cycle.
steps.body: Places are limited. Twelve weeks: heaviest at the start and the end, steady in between.

steps.title: Find your Pod.
steps.body: Month one: Pods of nine or more form around a problem situation. Everyone lands in one.

steps.title: Build with your team.
steps.body: Teams of three to five form around the projects you propose, with Mentors beside you.

steps.title: Show it. Pass it on.
steps.body: Show what you built at the Showcase, in public and open source. Then mentor, run a Pod, or bring the next person in.

how.markButton: Your Upskiller button, new this cycle

honest.$comment: Before the Apply button: what it is and isn't (a realistic preview; some people deciding it isn't for them is the point), then what happens next, dated. The dates, the application's questions and the contact are placeholders until they're set.
honest.title: What it is, and what it isn't.

items.title: No lectures.
items.body: Workshops teach skills, your Pod is where you practise, Mentors help when you're stuck, and you teach what you learn.

items.title: Not job placement.
items.body: You leave with credited open-source work, an audience at the Showcase, and people who've built with you.

items.title: In person.
items.body: Evenings at the library in DC, with some sessions online. Being in the room is most of it.

items.title: A real commitment.
items.body: Twelve weeks. Month one, while Pods form, and the run-up to the Showcase are the heaviest; the middle is steady. Most people feel unsure while Pods form, and everyone lands in one.

next.title: What happens next

steps.what: You hear back: a place, or the waitlist.

cycle.body: Twelve weeks, a Pod of curious peers, and a problem worth solving. Places are limited. It's an open cycle: the projects are open source, free for anyone to use and build on.

room.title: Pull up a chair.
room.body: It happens in person, at your library, with people figuring it out alongside you.
room.alt: A Labs evening at the library: people talking in small groups around the tables.

roles.title: Learn it. Then pass it on.
roles.lede: Upskillers learn by building. Mentors help a Pod past where it's stuck, and grow by doing it. Most people end up doing both: each cycle's Upskillers help the next one along. Both start with your free Upskilling account.

items.quote: The program gave me purpose again—connecting me with mission-driven public servants to tackle real problems.
items.name: Hector Perla

items.quote: I left realizing my gap is exactly where my strength lies—translating between tools, teams, and user needs.
items.name: Suzie Zhang

items.title: Founded in DC.
items.body: A pilot at the DC Public Library in the fall of 2025: a small group of 50 former federal workers, navigating career change and new technologies together. Now it's open to every professional.

items.title: Built to scale.
items.body: We run the Build Cycle on ourselves and turn what works into an operating system and playbooks, so a new Lab can start anywhere without reinventing it.

items.title: Expanding nationally.
items.body: From DC to cities across the country, wherever people are ready to learn by doing alongside their neighbors.

join.title: Find your people.
join.lede: The systems we've relied on are breaking. Here, you're invited to turn that disruption into resilience, rooted in your local library and powered by you and your neighbors.
join.note: Creates your free Upskilling account, with Google.
